Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a clinician who specializes in postpartum mental health. I’m here to make sure you’re getting the emotional support you deserve after having your baby.  

Today we’ll use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days, and it includes a question about self-harm so we can be sure you stay safe.  

Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free zone—there are no right or wrong answers, only what’s true for you. We’ll go through 10 gentle questions; each one asks how often you’ve experienced certain feelings. You can answer in your own words, and we can pause any time.  

Are you comfortable for us to begin?  

**First question:** Over the last seven days, how often have you found moments of joy or enjoyment in things—whether it’s your baby, a favorite show, a cup of coffee, anything at all?

I still smile at her little faces, but it’s… muted. Like, I’ll watch her stretch and yawn and my brain says “that’s beautiful,” yet the warm rush I used to feel is just a trickle. Most things—coffee, texting friends, even showering—feel flat, like I’m doing them on autopilot. I can count on one hand the minutes this week when I actually felt a spark.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really... I mean, my sister sent one of those silly memes and I tried to force a chuckle, but it felt fake. Nothing really lands as funny anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
Mostly I’m dreading things, honestly. I do look forward to my husband’s night feed so I can lie down, but even that feels more like relief than real enjoyment.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If she spits up more than usual, I immediately think it’s because I ate something “wrong.” When she wouldn’t settle at 3 a.m., I kept replaying every little choice—maybe I didn’t burp her long enough, maybe I’m just not good at this mom thing. I know in my head it’s probably normal baby stuff, but the guilt still jumps on me.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all the time. My mind keeps circling—Is she breathing? Did I fasten the car-seat strap too loose? Will she choke on her spit-up if I look away for a second? There’s no real trigger; the worry just rides along in the background, then spikes at night when the house is quiet.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week. It’ll hit out of nowhere—my heart races, I feel shaky, and suddenly I’m convinced something awful is about to happen, even though nothing’s going on. It usually passes if I pace the hallway or rock the baby, but it’s scary while it lasts.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like I’m treading water—feed, burp, change, laundry, sterilize—and the next wave’s already in my face. Sometimes I just sit on the couch staring at the mess, thinking I’ll never catch up. I still manage, but it’s overwhelming more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening several nights this week. I lie down exhausted, but my head starts spinning with worries about the baby, replaying everything I might’ve messed up, and this heavy sad feeling settles in my chest. It takes me over an hour to drift off, and then I jerk awake at every little sound thinking something’s wrong.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I feel that way most of the day. It’s like a gray cloud that just hangs there. I’ll be feeding her and tears start welling up for no clear reason—just this heavy, empty sadness that doesn’t lift much even when good things happen.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A couple of times this week. Yesterday I put her in the crib for a nap, sat down on the floor, and just started sobbing. Nothing specific triggered it—I just felt overwhelmed and hopeless, and the tears came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… it’s crossed my mind once or twice, mostly at night when I’m really drained. Nothing planned—just these flashes of “what if I weren’t here,” then I push it away because I know I’d never leave her. But the thoughts do pop up.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother (infant age not specified)  
Date: [today]

Symptoms endorsed  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia  
- Marked loss of enjoyment (forced laughter, anticipatory dread)  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame regarding infant care  
- Near-daily, non-triggered anxiety and panic spells (racing heart, shakiness)  
- Sleep-onset insomnia secondary to rumination and low mood  
- Frequent crying episodes without precipitant  
- Overwhelming sense of “treading water,” difficulty coping with routine tasks  
- Passive self-harm ideation (fleeting “what if I weren’t here,” no plan or intent)

Pattern  
Symptoms cluster in depressive (mood, pleasure, guilt, crying, sleep) and anxiety (free-floating worry, panic attacks) domains, consistent with moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety.

Risk flags  
– Passive suicidal thoughts (requires immediate safety assessment)  
– Significant functional impairment (self-care, household tasks)  
– Infant-care-related guilt and worry (potential impact on bonding)

Screening impression  
High clinical concern for major postpartum depressive episode with co-occurring anxiety; safety evaluation indicated today. Score and further assessment per clinician protocol; consider expedited referral to maternal mental health specialty services.
